summary: The 2014 landing page of Input, a family of fonts for code, is one short screen: a green masthead, a mosaic of live text tiles in editor themes (Lisp, HTML, Python, C++, a baseball table in box-drawing characters, a screenplay, a marine forecast, 'Code Beaches' in Input Sans) that swap places on a timer, a paragraph of intro and a link to the article. The preview tool, the info article and the download configurator are subpages that were not captured.

instances.look: Pale green page; 'INPUT™' in heavy green slab-like caps top-left, the italic tagline 'Fonts for code from DJR & Font Bureau' under it, a tab row 'Intro Preview Info Download' (current tab bold), and the DJR and Font Bureau logos in green at the far right
instances.feel: Plain, confident, a developer's tool page
instances.ux: Tabs go to the Preview tool, Info article and Download configurator subpages
instances.learn: For a utility font a masthead with four tabs can replace the hero: the samples below do the persuading

reconstruction.layout: Container 1152px centred (x=144); header ~155px: wordmark top-left (~80px cap height), tagline 14px below, nav row 12px with ~20px gaps; two 32px SVG logos right-aligned
reconstruction.typography: Wordmark Input Sans Narrow Black (or Serif) ~80px, uppercase, #00a000; tagline Input Serif Condensed Italic ~13px green; nav Input Sans Narrow ~13px, active item bold
reconstruction.assets: DJR and Font Bureau SVG logos

instances.look: A tight 4×3 mosaic of tiles, each a different text in its own editor theme: Racket/Lisp on navy, HTML in Monokai, a baseball standings table drawn with box characters, a JS function, a NASA screenplay, 'Code Beaches + California + New York + Washington' in Input Sans, Python in Solarized, C++ on dark teal, Ruby, 'Trapezoid / Diagonal / Semicircle' in large Input Serif, TeX, a 'SMALL CRAFT ADVISORY' marine forecast, a Unix 'top' process list
instances.feel: Busy, smart, like a wall of terminals
instances.ux: Tiles swap on a timer (tileswap.js): one tile at a time is replaced by another sample, so the mosaic keeps changing while you read
instances.learn: Show a coding font in every context a programmer meets (many languages, themes, data tables, prose, screenplays) as a self-shuffling mosaic of real text, not screenshots

reconstruction.layout: 1152×483 grid of 4 columns × 3 rows, tiles ~288×161px, no gutters, overflow hidden so code is cropped at the tile edges
reconstruction.typography: Code tiles ~11–12px in Input Mono / Mono Narrow / Mono Compressed with syntax colours per CodeMirror theme; 'Code Beaches' 44px Input Sans Compressed, list ~28px; 'Trapezoid…' ~40px Input Serif Condensed Light; screenplay in Input Mono with bold caps character names; forecast in Input Mono caps
reconstruction.behaviour: Interval-driven tile swap with a short transition (exact timing inferred from the video: a tile changes every ~1–2s); initial load shows tiles filling in
reconstruction.content: Real code (Racket pollen server, defcon/vanilla Python, C++ noordzij_cube), baseball standings, NASA screenplay, NOAA marine forecast, process list
reconstruction.assets: none (live text; CodeMirror themes: base16, monokai, solarized, lesser-dark, paraiso, xq-light, oldskool)

instances.look: Centred green paragraph in Input Sans 'Input is a flexible system of fonts designed specifically for code by David Jonathan Ross…' with an underlined designer link, then a bold underlined link 'See what makes Input a different coding typeface.'
instances.ux: The bold link opens the Info article subpage
instances.learn: One sentence on what is different (monospaced and proportional, many widths and weights) plus a link to the long argument is enough on a landing page

reconstruction.content: Real description of the Input family
